purpose: Complete XGTC session data-key installation when KEK changes, following the board original generators revealed by REA.

tooling.analysis: Local static decompilation, no target execution, external upload or global configuration changes

root_cause: Native session derivation updated KEK, OMCI IK and PLOAM IK but did not generate/install the two default data-key slots or replace their encrypted-key/key-name caches. After a previous Key-Control exchange, changing PON-TAG or MSK left cache contents generated under the preceding KEK; a subsequent confirmation could use the stale key-name cache. The original two session generators both call ca_generate_def_kek_and_kek_name after deriving KEK.
fix: Share the existing data-key generation/install operation between session initialization and Key-Control new-key requests.
Install both slots and replace their report caches before marking the new session ready.
Software slot validity tracks successful installation; downstream hardware validity still changes on a new-key request, so preparing defaults does not activate downstream keys prematurely.
Same-TAG fast path, Key-Control validation and original error propagation remain in effect.

scenarios: changed PON-TAG after seeded prior exchange
new MSK after seeded prior exchange
unchanged TAG does not regenerate keys
production Key-Control request and confirmation use the current slot
verification.scope: Actual stock key generators and native session-key function. Fixed synthetic RNG, generic OLT, synthetic registration/SN/TAG/MSK, real OpenSSL AES/CMAC; MMIO, locks and ACK update modeled. No live keys or optical execution.
verification.crypto: Real OpenSSL AES-128-ECB and AES-CMAC at the cryptographic boundaries for both original instruction replay and native code; deterministic synthetic RNG.
verification.after_comparison: KEK, PLOAM IK, OMCI IK, both encrypted keys, both key names and two data-key hardware slots match the original generator in all three derivation cases.

reviewed_without_changes: MSK/SK/IK register addresses and big-endian word packing match original setters.
No-message ACK body and MIC register packing match the original ACK path.
The original upstream GEM setter clears the global AES bit after its last encrypted user; no functional failure from the native owner policy was established here.
open_difference: Original MAC enable performs aal_psds_reset immediately before activation. Native initialization performs an earlier SerDes configuration/gearbox release. This turn does not establish equivalence or a failure from this ordering difference and does not alter it.
limits: Generic OLT fixture only; no CALIX-specific serial conversion exercised.
MMIO, RNG, locks and ACK update are modeled; no physical registration, key switching timing or encrypted traffic validation.
This finding does not establish the cause of the peer reported -110 or approximately50-second ACTP reset.
One targeted replay script and one ARM64 object build; no full tests, kernel link or full firmware build.
